usage.callShape: POST https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/chat/completions with JSON body {model, messages[], max_tokens}
usage.outputShape: body.choices[0].message.content (assistant text); actual served model in body.model; token usage in body.usage
quirks: This call returned HTTP 200 with NO payment required (free) despite the registry probe expecting 402 — pricing/gating appears request-dependent.

CRITICAL: the requested model 'nvidia/qwen3-coder-480b' was silently swapped for the free fallback 'nvidia/llama-4-maverick'. Response body.model came back 'nvidia/llama-4-maverick' and the content literally said 'I'm Llama 4 Maverick (Free)'. Always check body.model to confirm which model actually served — the qwen3-coder-480b id did not route to that model in this test.
Use model id 'nvidia/qwen3-coder-480b' per registry modelParam, but verify body.model in the response.
usage.guide: POST to https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/chat/completions with an OpenAI-style JSON body: {"model":"nvidia/qwen3-coder-480b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}]}. Read the assistant reply from body.choices[0].message.content. IMPORTANT: confirm body.model in the response matches what you requested — in QA testing the API silently fell back to the free 'nvidia/llama-4-maverick' model instead of serving qwen3-coder-480b. The call may come back free (200, no x402) or may require payment depending on the request; handle a 402 with x402 payment if it occurs.
